messages:
maria: Heads up — since ~09:10 UTC we've seen a sudden spike in dropped pod connections on ap-southeast-1 GPU pool (a100-pool). Affected services: model-serving, batch-prep. Symptoms: 502s from model pods, long RTOs, tcp resets.
kevin: On it. Any correlation with deployments or autoscaling events?
maria: Not matching deploys. Autoscaler did scale up a few nodes around 09:05. Node events show lots of SNAT allocations.
ryan: Running quick checks:
```
# conntrack entries
sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
> 262144
# nf_conntrack_max
sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
> 131072
```
kevin: Whoa that map is at 262k entries — higher than conntrack_max. Kernel dropping new entries and returning ESTABLISHED->RELATED resets probably. Any iptables SNAT churn?
zara: kube-proxy in ipvs mode on these nodes. Also calico NAT outgoing. I see many ephemeral src ports exhausted per node in ipvs stats.
maria: Packet captures show lots of SYN from pods with distinct src ports but replies get NAT collisions. Sample tcpdump:
```
tcpdump -nni eth0 port 443 and host 10.244.5.12
09:07:12.123456 IP 10.244.5.12.49152 > 3.120.45.10.443: S
...
09:07:12.223456 IP hostx.49152 > 3.120.45.10.443: R  # reset seen
```
ryan: Root cause theory: ephemeral port pool depletion / conntrack overflow from aggressive pod egress (many short-lived outbound connections for model artifacts). Each new SNAT mapping consumes conntrack; with scale-up we spike simultaneous connections.
kevin: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: increase nf_conntrack_max and enlarge ephemeral port range. Also reduce conntrack timeout for TCP_ESTABLISHED for these nodes.
zara: Proposed commands to run on affected ASG nodes (canary first):
```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="15000 61000"
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300
```
maria: Can we patch a kube-proxy/calico setting to avoid SNAT for intra-cluster pod->service traffic? Most egress is to external artifact hosts, but some is cluster-internal.
ryan: We already have externalSNAT disabled for some policies, but not all. Will add egress policy to use host networking for artifact fetcher pods and enable iptables --random-fully to reduce port collisions.
kevin: I'll open incident ticket and schedule rolling restart of kube-proxy on canary nodes after sysctl tweaks. infra-bot, create INC.
infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-345 created — "ap-southeast-1 SNAT/conntrack exhaustion causing pod disconnects". Severity P2. Linking node list and recent autoscale events.
maria: After sysctl bump & kube-proxy restart on 3 canary nodes, errors dropped to near-zero in that AZ. Monitoring continuing. Next steps: make conntrack_max change ASG-wide via launch-template; long-term: implement SNAT pool per node via SNAT manager or use AWS NAT gateway for heavy egress.
zara: Also adding instrumentation: per-node conntrack meter to alert at 70% and ephemeral port usage alert. I'll add runbook steps for on-call.
kevin: Thanks team. I'll roll the sysctl change via sudo-run on remaining nodes and trigger infra PR for launch-template. Follow-up in 30m.
maria: TL;DR — root cause: conntrack / ephemeral port exhaustion during scale-up; mitigations: increase nf_conntrack_max, expand ephemeral range, reduce conntrack timeouts, use host networking or NAT gateway for heavy egress, instrument alerts. :thumbsup:
kevin: Closing thread when incident updates are posted to INC.
